sentences.text:
Shri Hakim Khan Qureshi, learned counsel for appellants  Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Government Advocate for  respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No3761 of 2025 , which is third application under Section 430(1) of B.N.S.S., 2023 on behalf of the appellant No.2- Kamlakant Gautam @ Bablu for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
His first application was dismissed as withdrawn and second application was dismissed as infructuous.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction and sentence dated 27.02.2021 passed by the First Additional Sessions Judge, Maihar District Satna in S.T. No.125/2017, whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
 Conviction U/s. 
 Imprisonment Fine  
 302 (three Life Rs.10,000/- (three  
 counts) of IPC Imprisonment count)
 498A of IPC RI for 5 years Rs.5,000/-

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Maihar District Satna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant No.2.
He further submits that Vindhyeshwari and her two sons, who were respectively wife and sons of appellant No.2-Kamlakant Gautam, died in her matrimonial home due to burn injuries.
It is submitted that as per evidence of Pooja Dwivedi (PW-3), 2 CRA-1640-2021 Kamlakant had lived his parental home to drop Pooja Dwivedi to her matrimonial home at Harai.

PW-4 and PW-5 have also given statements that when Kamlakant had visited at Harai to drop Pooja Dwivedi then he had received a call that his house was put on fire when he had rushed back to his home Shivshankar Gautam @ Lalli vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81043041/
1 town.

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that as far as Kamlakant is concerned, prosecution has admitted his absence from the scene of crime, which is also corroborated from his memorandum Ex.P/16 so also independent prosecution witnesses who were declared hostile.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed on the ground of parity.
Learned Government Advocate, on the other hand, has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant No.2-Kamlakant Gautam @ Bablu can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, I.A. No.3761/2026 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant No.2-Kamlakant Gautam @ Bablu is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this 3 CRA-1640-2021 Court on 04.03.2026 and on such other dates,
as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing as per its turn and seniority.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (RATNESH CHANDRA SING  JUDGE JUDGE  RS Shivshankar Gautam @ Lalli vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81043041/
